title: Simple Homotopy, Whitehead Groups, and Torsion

items.title: Elementary expansions and collapses of finite CW complexes
items.statement: For a finite CW complex X, an elementary expansion X↪Y attaches an (n−1,n)-cell pair (n≥1) such that the new (n−1)-cell is a specified free face of the new n-cell and the characteristic map meets it by a homeomorphism. Equivalently Y=X∪_q D^n with q on an upper hemisphere; the pair deformation retracts onto X. An elementary collapse is a deformation retraction removing such a pair; the operation is taken componentwise and fixes the retained subcomplex.

items.title: Simple homotopy equivalence
items.statement: A map f:X→Y between finite CW complexes is a simple homotopy equivalence when it is homotopic to a finite composite of elementary expansions, elementary collapses and cellular isomorphisms between finite CW complexes. For disconnected spaces the sequence respects the induced component bijection; every such map is a homotopy equivalence. No arbitrary homeomorphism is included by definition.

items.title: Stable general linear and elementary groups for right modules
items.statement: Let R be any associative unital ring, possibly noncommutative. On the free right module R^n with column coordinates v=Σ e_j v_j, a right-linear map has matrix A acting by Av, so (Av)_i=Σ_j A_ij v_j and composition is ordinary matrix multiplication in the displayed order. Define GL_n(R) by two-sided invertible n×n matrices, stabilize by A↦diag(A,1), and let GL(R)=colim GL_n(R). Define E(R) to be the subgroup generated by e_ij(r)=I+rE_ij (i≠j) after stabilization; these matrices are invertible with inverse e_ij(−r). This construction uses no commutativity or determinant.

items.title: Stable elementary matrices equal the commutator subgroup
items.statement: For every associative unital ring R, E(R) is normal in GL(R) and E(R)=[GL(R),GL(R)]. Thus GL(R)/E(R) is abelian. The equality holds after stabilization, and neither side relies on a determinant.
items.proof_strategy: For distinct i,j,k, [e_ij(r),e_jk(1)]=e_ik(r), giving E⊆[GL,GL]. Conversely stabilize A,B∈GL_n to 2n×2n; multiply by block elementary shears to show diag(AB,I) and diag(BA,I) are equivalent modulo E. The signed block interchange [[0,−I],[I,0]] is a product of elementary shears. Hence AB and BA have the same class modulo E; in particular A e A^{-1}∈E for e∈E, establishing normality, and every commutator lies in E. Track matrix multiplication in the noncommutative order; the identities are the ones in Lück Lemma 2.2.

items.title: K₁ of a ring and the Whitehead group of a discrete group
items.statement: Write K₁(R)=GL(R)/E(R) additively, so [AB]=[A]+[B] and [I]=0. Let K̃₁(R)=K₁(R)/⟨[−1]⟩. For any discrete group π, put Wh(π)=K₁(Z[π])/⟨[±g]:g∈π⟩, equivalently K̃₁(Z[π])/⟨[g]⟩. The classes of group elements refer to 1×1 unit matrices. A group homomorphism induces maps on group rings, K₁ and Wh; inner automorphisms of π induce the identity on Wh.

items.title: Integral group rings have invariant basis number
items.statement: For every discrete π, R=Z[π] has invariant basis number: an isomorphism of finite free right R-modules R^m≅R^n forces m=n. More generally, this holds for a unital ring admitting a unital homomorphism to a nonzero commutative ring with invariant basis number.
items.proof_strategy: Represent a hypothetical right-linear isomorphism R^m→R^n and its inverse by rectangular matrices A,B with AB=I_n and BA=I_m. Apply the augmentation ε:Z[π]→Z entrywise; ε(A),ε(B) are inverse rectangular integer matrices. Thus Z^m≅Z^n, and invariant basis number for Z gives m=n. No determinant over the possibly noncommutative group ring is invoked.

items.title: A chain contraction makes the odd-to-even parity map invertible
items.statement: Let C be a bounded finite free right R-chain complex and s a right-linear contraction, ds+sd=1. The odd-to-even and even-to-odd components of d+s are inverse isomorphisms up to finite unipotent corrections; in particular (d+s)_odd:C_odd→C_even is an isomorphism of right R-modules. This holds over arbitrary unital R, without a rank or invariant-basis-number assumption.
items.proof_strategy: On the total Z/2-graded module, (d+s)^2=ds+sd+s²=1+s². Since s² strictly raises homological degree by two and C is bounded, s² is nilpotent and 1+s² has the finite inverse Σ_{j≥0}(−s²)^j. This even operator commutes with d+s because it is its square. Hence (d+s)^{-1}=(d+s)(1+s²)^{-1}; both parity components are inverse module isomorphisms. The rank issue is left to the next definition.

items.title: Finite based free complexes and contraction torsion
items.statement: For a bounded chain complex C of finite based free right R-modules with a specified right-linear contraction s, order the concatenated odd- and even-degree bases by degree, and let Φ_s=(d+s)_odd:C_odd→C_even. When the two displayed finite bases have equal size, define τ_s(C)=[Φ_s]∈K̃₁(R) in additive notation. This size condition is automatic if R has invariant basis number, in particular for R=Z[π]. Over an arbitrary non-IBN ring the matrix formula is asserted only when the displayed basis sizes agree. The odd-to-even parity convention is fixed here; its choice yields τ(0→R --u→R→0)=[u] when the upper degree is odd.

items.title: Contraction torsion does not depend on the contraction
items.statement: Under the basis-size hypothesis in the definition, any two right-linear contractions s,t of the same bounded based free complex C give τ_s(C)=τ_t(C) in K̃₁(R). Denote their common value by τ(C).
items.proof_strategy: Order summands by degree. Compare (d+s)_odd with the inverse of (d+t)_even using the finite operators μ_n=(s_{n+1}−t_{n+1})t_n and ν_n=(t_{n+1}−s_{n+1})s_n. Directly expand ds+sd=dt+td=1: the resulting comparison products are upper triangular by degree with identity diagonal, as in Lück equation (2.7). Each such finite unipotent triangular matrix is a product of elementary matrices, hence class zero in K₁. The two parity maps yield opposite classes; eliminating the even map proves the odd classes equal. The possible block-ordering signs vanish in K̃₁ by construction.

items.title: Basis-change, direct-sum and based exact-sequence formulas
items.statement: For bounded contractible based free right R-complexes with defined torsion, τ(C⊕D)=τ(C)+τ(D). If the new degree-n basis is the old basis multiplied by P_n on the right in column coordinates, then τ_new(C)=τ_old(C)+Σ_n(−1)^{n+1}[P_n] in K̃₁(R). For a degreewise based exact sequence 0→C→D→E→0 of contractible complexes whose middle basis is the concatenation of the sub- and quotient bases, τ(D)=τ(C)+τ(E). For a strictly commutative based exact diagram of bounded finite based free chain complexes with two vertical chain homotopy equivalences and equal odd/even displayed basis counts in each of the three mapping cones, τ(g)=τ(f)+τ(h) for the middle, sub- and quotient maps, where τ(v):=τ(Cone(v)) with target-first cone bases. The row complexes need not be contractible. For a degreewise based chain isomorphism f:C→D, the mapping-cone torsion is τ(f)=Σ_n(−1)^n[f_n] in K̃₁(R), with each f_n written in the displayed bases.
items.proof_strategy: Block direct sum gives the first identity. The basis formula follows from Φ_new=P_even^{-1}Φ_old P_odd, so the odd matrices contribute +[P_n] and even matrices −[P_n]. For the exact sequence, take a degreewise splitting of D→E from the displayed quotient basis. A contraction of E corrects it to a chain splitting by s=dσs_E+σs_Ed. The resulting C⊕E→D is an isomorphism with upper unipotent degreewise matrices; compare contractions and apply the basis formula. For chain maps, apply this to the corresponding based exact sequence of mapping cones. The only use of contractibility is explicit; ordinary acyclicity is not substituted. For the final chain-isomorphism formula, identify Cone(f) with Cone(1_C) using f on the target summands, apply the alternating basis-change formula, and note that Cone(1_C) has the explicit zero-torsion elementary contraction.

items.title: Based cellular chains of a universal cover as finite free right group-ring modules
items.statement: Let X be a connected finite CW complex with x∈X, π=π₁(X,x), and chosen universal cover p:X̃→X. Use the library’s traversal-order deck isomorphism g↦T_g and define the right R=Z[π] action on cellular chains by c·g=T_g^{-1}c, extended Z-linearly. Choose an orientation, order and one oriented lift of each cell of X. Then C_n^{cell}(X̃;Z)=H_n(X̃^n,X̃^{n−1};Z) is finite based free right R on those lifts. For a CW pair (X,A), use the lifts of relative cells for C_n^{cell}(X̃,p^{-1}A;Z). Empty degrees are zero and disconnected finite complexes are treated componentwise.

items.title: Cellular basis ambiguities vanish in the Whitehead group
items.statement: Elementary basis changes of finite right R-modules have class zero in K₁(R); reordering bases changes K₁ only by [−1]. For R=Z[π], reversing a cell orientation or replacing its chosen lift changes one basis vector by a unit ±g, hence has class zero in Wh(π). A change of basepoint path conjugates π and acts trivially on Wh(π). These are distinct quotients: an arbitrary unit of Z[π] need not be killed.
items.proof_strategy: Elementary changes are E(R) by definition. A transposition is a product of elementary shears and one diagonal −1; any finite permutation is a product of transpositions. A deck lift changes by T_g, which under the right action is multiplication by g^{-1}; orientation contributes −1. The alternating basis formula from the preceding lemma reduces every such change to a sum of [±g]. For an inner automorphism h↦ghg^{-1}, its action on matrices is conjugation by the 1×1 unit g on each free summand; in abelian K₁ this has zero net class, so path transport is independent of the chosen path.

items.title: Universal-cover boundaries, maps and homotopies respect the right group-ring action
items.statement: Cellular boundaries on a universal cover are right Z[π]-linear. For a based cellular map f:(X,x)→(Y,y) inducing a π₁-isomorphism and compatible chosen basepoint lifts, its lifted cellular chain map is right Z[π₁Y]-linear after source coefficient transport by f_*. A lifted cellular homotopy, which may move the basepoint, yields a right-linear chain homotopy between the initial lifted map and the endpoint lift after its deck twist, with both maps using the initial f_* transport. The deck transformation by itself need not be right-linear for a nonabelian group.
items.proof_strategy: Use naturality of connecting maps for cellular boundaries. A based compatible lift intertwines deck actions through f_*; a different lift conjugates that identification. Lift the cellular homotopy from its initial lift; uniqueness gives deck equivariance throughout, so the cellular prism is right-linear for f_* and ends at the deck-twisted lift of the final map. Only the composite endpoint map is asserted right-linear.

items.title: A lifted finite CW equivalence has a contractible group-ring mapping cone
items.statement: For a based homotopy equivalence f:(X,x)→(Y,y) of connected finite CW complexes, choose a based cellular representative and compatible universal-cover lifts. After transporting source coefficients through f_*:π₁X≅π₁Y, the right Z[π₁Y]-chain map C_*(f̃) is a chain-homotopy equivalence. Its algebraic cone, with C_n(f)=C_n(Ỹ)⊕C_{n−1}(X̃) and the published cone differential, is bounded finite based free and contractible. The proof uses based deformation retracts of the finite cellular mapping cylinder and does not infer contractibility from homology vanishing.
items.proof_strategy: In the finite cellular mapping cylinder M_f, both endpoint inclusions are homotopy equivalences; the target has its explicit strong deformation retract and the source has one by the CW inclusion theorem. Make the retracts and homotopies cellular relative to the fixed endpoint subcomplexes. Choose lifts in the universal cover of M_f along the source prism path; the lifted based deformations commute with the common deck group and give right-linear cellular chain homotopies for both inclusions over Z[π₁M_f]≅Z[π₁Y]. The compatible lift of f factors as the lifted collapse after the lifted source inclusion, hence its chain map has a right-linear homotopy inverse. Apply the published cone criterion and finite-cell bases.

items.title: Whitehead torsion of a finite CW homotopy equivalence
items.statement: For f:X→Y a homotopy equivalence of connected finite CW complexes, choose a based cellular representative, compatible universal-cover lifts and cellular bases; let π=π₁(Y), transport C_*(X̃) from Z[π₁X] to Z[π] via f_*, and define τ(f) as the image in Wh(π) of the reduced contraction torsion τ(Cone(C_*(f̃))). The cone uses C_n(Ỹ)⊕C_{n−1}(X̃), with target summands first. For disconnected Y, τ(f) lies in ⊕_{D∈π₀Y}Wh(π₁D) componentwise. This is a chosen-data definition; the next theorem proves independence.

items.title: Whitehead torsion is independent of all auxiliary choices
items.statement: The class τ(f) is independent of the contraction, orientations, orders, cell lifts, universal-cover identifications, basepoint paths and cellular approximation. For a target basepoint change y→y′, τ(f) transports under the canonical Wh(π₁(Y,y))→Wh(π₁(Y,y′)) isomorphism; different paths induce the same map because they differ by inner conjugation. Homotopic finite CW homotopy equivalences have equal torsion after this canonical transport.
items.proof_strategy: Contraction independence is the preceding lemma. Orientation, order and lift changes are signed monomial matrices; use the alternating basis-change formula and the quotient by [±g]. A different lift of f̃ differs by a deck unit on the target, likewise killed. Two cellular approximations are homotopic by a finite cellular homotopy; its lifted prism is right-linear after basepoint-track transport. The published mapping-cone isomorphism for homotopic chain maps is a degreewise unipotent triangular shear, so its torsion is zero by the basis-change formula. Basepoint paths induce conjugate π-identifications; show inner conjugation fixes K₁(Z[π]) by conjugation with diag(g,…,g) and abelianness. Apply componentwise for disconnected finite complexes.

items.title: Composition and based-pair sum formulas for Whitehead torsion
items.statement: For finite CW homotopy equivalences f:X→Y and g:Y→Z, τ(g∘f)=τ(g)+g_*τ(f) in Wh(π₁Z) (componentwise if disconnected), where g_* transports Wh(π₁Y) through the induced group isomorphism. For a cellular map of finite CW pairs f:(X,A)→(Y,B) whose full and subspace maps are homotopy equivalences, and with basepoint/component data fixed, the based exact cone sequence gives τ(f_X)=j_*τ(f_A)+τ(f_{rel}) in Wh(π₁Y), where the relative cone is formed from the actual lifted pairs (X̃,p_X^{-1}A) and (Ỹ,p_Y^{-1}B) over Z[π₁Y], and j:B↪Y induces componentwise coefficient extension. Equivalently, in any based exact diagram of contractible relative complexes, torsion of the middle is the sum of subobject and quotient torsions.
items.proof_strategy: Use the algebraic composition formula for finite based free chain equivalences (Lück, Lemma 2.9), transporting coefficient rings through g_*. For the pair formula use the degreewise based exact rows 0→C_*(p_X^{-1}A)→C_*(X̃)→C_*(X̃,p_X^{-1}A)→0 and its Y/B analogue, then take mapping cones of the vertical maps. The lifted A/B subcomplex chain maps are scalar extensions of the component universal-cover maps, even when π₁B→π₁Y is not injective. Prove the quotient cone contractible by correcting a graded section with a contraction of the subcone. Apply the based exact torsion sum and identify the subcone term as j_*τ(f_A).

items.title: An elementary CW expansion has zero Whitehead torsion
items.statement: If j:X↪Y is an elementary expansion of finite CW complexes, τ(j)=0 in Wh(π₁Y), componentwise. In suitable oriented lifts the only nonzero relative cellular boundary is R --±g→R in consecutive degrees, where g∈π₁Y; it is a contractible two-term complex and [±g]=0 in Wh(π₁Y).
items.proof_strategy: The target inclusion induces π₁-isomorphism and is a homotopy equivalence by the free-face deformation. The universal-cover pair has one orbit of each new cell, and the incidence of the specified free face is a single unit ±g; no other relative cells occur. The relative cone quotient of the mapping cone has this two-term based complex, while the source identity cone has torsion zero. Apply the based-pair sum formula and the definition of Wh to conclude τ(j)=0. The parity sign does not matter because [±g] is killed.

items.title: Simple homotopy equivalences have zero torsion
items.statement: Every simple homotopy equivalence f:X→Y of finite CW complexes has τ(f)=0 in the correctly transported target Whitehead group.
items.proof_strategy: An elementary expansion has zero by the preceding lemma. Its collapse retraction r satisfies rj≃1, so the composition identity and isomorphism of transported Wh groups give τ(r)=0. A cellular isomorphism induces signed monomial matrices on based universal-cover cellular chains; the basis-change formula and ±g quotient give torsion zero. Add the torsions of a finite composite with transport to each successive target, and use homotopy invariance for f. Treat connected components separately.

items.title: The target of a finite cellular mapping cylinder is a simple subcomplex
items.statement: For any cellular map f:X→Y of finite CW complexes, the target inclusion i_Y:Y↪M_f is a finite composite of elementary expansions. If f is a homotopy equivalence, the source inclusion i_X:X↪M_f is a homotopy equivalence, and τ(f)=p_*τ(i_X) for the canonical retraction p:M_f→Y; p is a homotopy inverse of i_Y, is homotopic relative to Y to a finite composite of elementary collapse maps, and has zero torsion.
items.proof_strategy: Give M_f the published cellular cylinder structure. Order the cells of X by dimension; for each source n-cell, its prism D^n×I and its exposed n-dimensional top form a free (n,n+1)-cell pair attached to the cylinder already built from lower source cells and Y. Attach these pairs successively, proving i_Y simple. The retraction p satisfies p i_Y=1 and i_Y p≃1; the composition formula gives τ(p)=0. Since p i_X=f, apply composition with target transport to obtain τ(f)=p_*τ(i_X). This is the required reduction of the converse to an inclusion. Reverse the expansion sequence to obtain a collapse composite r fixing Y; composing the cylinder deformation H from 1 to i_Y p with r gives rH from r to p relative to Y.

items.title: Cell trading puts a finite relative equivalence in two high degrees
items.statement: Let L⊂K be finite connected CW complexes with inclusion a homotopy equivalence. Relative to L, finitely many elementary expansions and collapses transform (K,L) into (K′,L) whose relative cells occur only in two adjacent degrees n,n+1 with n≥3. The deformation respects the homotopy class and transports the relative torsion. The low-dimensional 0- and 1-cell cases are included, using connectedness and the induced π₁-isomorphism.
items.proof_strategy: Use the relative homotopy exact sequence to get π_r(K,L)=0 for all r≥1 and component bijection. Following Cohen §7.3, choose a relative cell of least degree r. Its characteristic disk is homotopic rel its attaching boundary into L; for r=0 use a path in L and for r=1 use π₁-surjectivity/injectivity to close the required path. Use HEP to make the disk homotopy cellular and attach a new (r+1,r+2) elementary pair whose (r+1)-cell provides a free face opposite the old r-cell. Collapse that old cell with its new partner; the remaining new cell has higher dimension. Repeat for the finite list, increasing the minimum degree, and, when needed, use an additional finite trading round to arrange a common adjacent pair n,n+1 above degree two and above the old relative dimension. Cohen §7.4 counts cells and verifies termination and equality of two layer ranks; every move fixes L. No infinite selection or AC is needed.

items.title: Two high relative cell layers have free homotopy bases and their cellular boundary matrix
items.statement: Let L⊂K be connected finite CW complexes, π₁(L)→π₁(K) an isomorphism, and suppose the relative cells occur only in dimensions n,n+1 with n≥3. Put K_n=L plus the n-cells and R=Z[π₁K]. Then π_n(K_n,L) and π_{n+1}(K,K_n) are finite free right R-modules on the chosen oriented characteristic cells, up to ±g. The triple boundary ∂:π_{n+1}(K,K_n)→π_n(K_n,L) is represented in those bases by the relative cellular differential d_{n+1}:C_{n+1}(K̃,L̃)→C_n(K̃,L̃). If L↪K is a homotopy equivalence, ∂ is an isomorphism, hence its matrix is invertible.
items.proof_strategy: The π₁-isomorphism makes the preimage L̃ in the universal cover K̃ connected and simply connected; attaching only cells of degree ≥3 preserves this for K̃_n. Apply the published choice-free single-layer homotopy/homology basis lemma separately to (K̃_n,L̃) and (K̃,K̃_n). Deck translates of each chosen lift give the right R basis (with action c·g=T_g^{-1}c), and relative Hurewicz naturality makes the triple boundary commute with the cellular homology boundary, coefficient by coefficient and with disk-orientation signs. For a homotopy-equivalence inclusion, π_*(K,L)=0; exactness of the published triple sequence gives ∂ bijective. Degree n≥3 avoids the nonabelian relative π₂ module defect noted by Cohen §8.1.

items.title: Cell slides and elementary pairs realize stable group-ring matrix operations
items.statement: For a homotopy-equivalence inclusion L⊂K of finite connected CW complexes with relative cells only in degrees n,n+1, n≥3, finite elementary expansions and collapses fixing L realize A↦PAQ and A↦diag(A,I_m) for elementary P,Q over R=Z[π₁L], where A is its relative boundary matrix in column coordinates on right R-modules. Permutations and factors ±g are realized by reordering, reorienting or changing lifts of characteristic cells. Thus every stable elementary matrix operation used in K₁ can be implemented geometrically without changing the pair’s relative simple type.

references.title: Lurie, Theorem 8 sketch and Remark 12, pp.3–4

items.proof_strategy: First trivialize lower attaching maps inside L using the induced π_{n−1}-isomorphism and finite attaching-map collars (Cohen §§7.1, 7.4). For an elementary right factor I+E_{ij}r in the column convention, form a new upper attaching sphere θ representing [φ_j]+[φ_i]r using finite pinch and whisker maps. Because the ith upper cell fills φ_i, θ and φ_j are homotopic in the subcomplex containing all cells except the jth upper cell; Cohen §8.3 realizes their replacement by an elementary expansion/collapse. This changes exactly the jth boundary column by A_i r, giving A(I+E_{ij}r). A disjoint free-face pair gives diag(A,1). Since A is invertible and E(R) normal, PA=A(A^{-1}PA) converts each opposite-side elementary factor into finitely many upper slides, as in Cohen §8.4. Orientations, lifts and order changes give units and permutations. All moves fix L.

items.title: Identity relative boundary matrix permits geometric cancellation
items.statement: If a connected finite CW pair (K,L) has only relative n- and (n+1)-cells with n≥3 and its relative boundary matrix is the identity in chosen group-ring homotopy bases, then (K,L) is equivalent rel L by a finite sequence of elementary expansions and collapses to (L,L). Equality of homology incidence alone is not used as a free-face criterion; the attaching maps are first corrected in relative homotopy.
items.proof_strategy: By the preceding free homotopy basis lemma, identity columns say that the boundary class of each upper characteristic disk equals the class of its matching lower characteristic cell, with no other lower-cell terms. Use a based relative homotopy and HEP to replace its attaching map by one whose sphere has the matching lower-cell disk as a genuine free face, through a mapping-cylinder elementary expansion followed by collapse; Cohen §8.2 writes this characteristic-map homotopy explicitly. Collapse that upper/lower pair. The remaining relative homotopy matrix is again an identity of one smaller size, since coefficients for the removed row and column are zero. Repeat finitely to reach L. This step is geometric and retains all attaching-map hypotheses.

items.title: Zero relative Whitehead torsion yields a finite relative elementary deformation
items.statement: Let L⊂K be a homotopy-equivalence inclusion of finite connected CW complexes. If τ(L↪K)=0 in Wh(π₁K), then K reduces to L by finitely many elementary expansions and collapses relative to L, with only orientation, lift and order changes of the cell bases. This is the hard geometric converse for inclusions and is proved independently of the final if-and-only-if theorem.
items.proof_strategy: Cell-trade the pair to two adjacent degrees n,n+1≥3. The pair torsion is, up to the fixed parity sign, the class of its invertible relative boundary matrix A; the finite elementary moves preserve this class by the sum/composition formula. Vanishing in Wh means that after block stabilization, A is a product of elementary matrices and diagonal trivial units ±g (normality and the K₁ quotient were established earlier). Change orientations/lifts to absorb ±g, then realize each elementary factor by the cell-slide lemma, reducing A to an identity matrix; stabilization is a finite expansion. The identity-matrix cancellation lemma then removes all relative cells. Cohen §8.5 proves this reduction, with §8.2 supplying the geometric last step; the proof does not infer a free face from acyclicity alone.

items.title: Every Whitehead class is realized by a finite CW homotopy equivalence
items.statement: Let X be a connected finite CW complex, π=π₁X and η∈Wh(π). There is a finite CW complex Y containing X as a subcomplex such that i:X↪Y is a homotopy equivalence and i_*^{-1}τ(i)=η. One can take the relative cells in two consecutive degrees n,n+1 with n≥3, and no new cells below degree three. For disconnected X, realize a class on each of finitely many components separately.
items.proof_strategy: Choose an invertible A∈GL_m(Z[π]) representing η and choose an even n≥max(4,dim X+1) so the upper degree n+1 is odd and the torsion sign is positive; stabilization allows m≥1. Attach m trivially based n-cells to X. Their absolute wedge-sphere classes and π-translates map onto the free relative homotopy basis, so every column of A is represented by a based attaching map S^n→X∨(∨S^n); attach m (n+1)-cells along those maps. The universal-cover relative cellular complex is 0→R^m --A→R^m→0, hence contractible. Its relative integral homology vanishes. The pair of universal covers has simply connected base and is 1-connected. If a relative π_k were first nonzero, the choice-free relative Hurewicz comparison at that least k would identify it with the zero H_k, contradiction; thus all relative π vanish. Covering π_k-isomorphisms transfer this to (Y,X), and the finite clause of the published Whitehead theorem makes i a homotopy equivalence without AC. The pair/cone formula and the odd-degree convention give τ(i)=[A]=η after identifying π₁Y=π.

items.title: Whitehead torsion is the complete obstruction to finite CW simple homotopy
items.statement: A homotopy equivalence f:X→Y of finite CW complexes is simple if and only if τ(f)=0 in ⊕_{D∈π₀Y}Wh(π₁D), with each summand canonically transported under basepoint changes. No smooth handle, Whitney or s-cobordism assertion is part of this theorem.
items.proof_strategy: The forward implication is the separate simple-implies-zero theorem. For the reverse, first use homotopy invariance to make f cellular. The target inclusion Y↪M_f is simple, so its inverse retraction p has zero torsion; the composition formula gives τ(f)=p_*τ(X↪M_f). Since p_* is an isomorphism, the source inclusion has zero torsion. Apply the separate hard relative zero-torsion lemma to collapse M_f to X by finite elementary moves fixing X. Thus X↪M_f is simple; compose with p and the homotopy f=p∘i_X to conclude f simple. Do this independently on the finitely many components.

title: Simple Homotopy, Whitehead Groups, and Torsion: Examples

items.title: A free-face interval expansion has zero torsion
items.statement: Starting from one vertex X={v}, attach a new vertex w and a 1-cell e from v to w. The new vertex is a free face, so X↪Y is an elementary expansion. Relative universal-cover chains have 0→Z⟨e⟩ --1→ Z⟨w⟩→0, giving τ(X↪Y)=0 in Wh(1). The same computation over any π gives the boundary unit ±g and zero Whitehead class.
items.proof_strategy: List the two new cells, choose the orientation from v to w, and compute the relative cellular boundary of e as w after quotienting X. The contraction sends w to e. The odd-to-even parity map is the 1×1 matrix (1), so its K₁ and Wh class is zero. Apply the general expansion lemma for arbitrary π and sign/lift choices.

items.title: The Whitehead group of the trivial group is zero
items.statement: For the trivial group 1, Z[1]=Z and K₁(Z)≅{±1} by the determinant. Since Wh(1)=K₁(Z)/⟨[−1]⟩, one has Wh(1)=0. Consequently every finite simply connected CW homotopy equivalence has zero torsion and is simple by the main theorem.
items.proof_strategy: Over Z, any invertible matrix has primitive first column. Apply the integer Euclidean algorithm/Bézout operations as elementary row matrices to reduce that column to (±1,0,…,0); clear its row and iterate on the remaining minor. Stabilized signed permutations are elementary modulo [−1]. Thus every K₁(Z) class is represented by ±1, while the ordinary integer determinant sends these two classes to distinct units. The Whitehead quotient kills the negative unit. Cite the main theorem only for the final consequence; the group computation itself does not depend on it.

items.title: Torsion of a two-term based contractible complex
items.statement: Let R be unital, u∈R×, and C be 0→C_q=R --u→ C_{q−1}=R→0 for q≥1 with the displayed ordered right bases. Then C is contractible. With the odd-to-even convention, τ(C)=(-1)^{q+1}[u]∈K̃₁(R): [u] if q is odd and −[u] if q is even. After passing to Wh(π), the same formula holds for R=Z[π].
items.proof_strategy: Take s_{q−1}=u^{-1} and all other s_j=0; verify ds+sd=1 on the two nonzero modules. If q is odd, (d+s)_odd is multiplication by u; if q is even, it is multiplication by u^{-1}. Thus its class is [u] or −[u] respectively. Independence of the chosen contraction follows from the A-page lemma, and [−1] absorbs any basis-parity permutation sign.

items.title: Ordinary acyclicity forgets nonzero group-ring torsion
items.statement: Let π=C₅=⟨t∣t⁵=1⟩ and R=Z[π]. The element u=1−t²−t³ is a unit with inverse v=1−t−t⁴, but u is not ±t^k. The based two-term right R-complex 0→R --u→R→0 is contractible and therefore acyclic even after forgetting to abelian groups, while its torsion [u] is nonzero in Wh(C₅). Indeed determinant on the commutative ring R maps the Whitehead quotient to R×/⟨±t^k⟩ and detects u. There is also a finite CW homotopy equivalence with this nonzero torsion, hence it is not simple.
items.proof_strategy: Multiply u(1−t−t⁴) in Z[t]/(t⁵−1) and collect coefficients to obtain 1; inspect coefficients of u to see it is not a monomial ±t^k. Because C₅ is abelian, R is commutative, and the determinant of an invertible matrix respects products and sends elementary matrices to 1. It therefore descends to K₁(R) and then to the displayed quotient of units. The degree-one two-term computation gives τ=[u], whose determinant class is nontrivial. Invoke the A-page realization lemma and the main iff theorem for the geometric non-simple example. This demonstrates that vanishing ordinary homology does not erase the basis and group-ring data carried by torsion.
